title: Add data freshness indicators (timestamp, lag warnings, partial-data banner) to Usage Insights
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
Add end-to-end support (API + Console UI) to show data freshness for Usage Insights. This includes (1) a freshness timestamp, (2) lag warnings when aggregation is behind expected SLAs, and (3) partial-data banners when results may be incomplete due to late events/backfills/region-level ingestion issues.

Why: During beta, customers and internal teams have raised concerns about totals shifting and short-term mismatches vs billing when the underlying aggregated dataset is still catching up. We need clear, consistent messaging so engineers/FinOps can trust what they’re seeing (and know when not to).
requirements:
API requirements:
- All Usage Insights query endpoints should return freshness metadata alongside the results.
- Freshness should include the max event time covered and the computed lag relative to “now” for the requested workspace/project filter.
- API should indicate if results are partial for the requested time range due to known ingestion gaps or aggregation backfill in progress.
- API should be consistent across breakdown and top drivers endpoints.

Console requirements:
- Show “Data as of <timestamp>” in the page header for Usage → Cost → Usage Insights.
- If lag exceeds threshold, show a warning banner with the lag amount and link to help article.
- If results are partial, show a prominent banner that explains what is missing and how that might affect totals (e.g., ‘some regions are delayed’, ‘late events still processing’).
- Banners should be sticky at top of insights view, but not block table interaction.
- When exporting CSV, include the same “data as of” timestamp in the export metadata (filename and/or first line comment) so finance workflows can reconcile later.

Non-goals:
- Do not implement new data-quality dashboards here (tracked in SRE/observability work).
- Do not attempt to “fix” lag; this ticket only surfaces and explains it.
acceptance_criteria:
1) API: /usage-insights/* endpoints include fields for freshness timestamp and lag, and a partial-data indicator.
2) Console header displays “Data as of …” using the API-provided timestamp (not client time).
3) Lag warning banner appears when lag is above threshold and includes the lag value (e.g., ‘~27 min behind’).
4) Partial-data banner appears when API indicates partial results; banner copy matches docs/DevEx guidance.
5) Export flow: exported CSV contains the same “data as of” timestamp and partial-data status (either header comments or export manifest fields).
6) E2E test(s): simulate stale/partial response and verify UI states.
7) Copy reviewed by PM + DevEx (avoid scary language; be explicit about implications).
implementation_notes:
Proposed API contract (align with Confluence API standards doc):
- Add to query responses:
  - freshness_as_of: RFC3339 timestamp (UTC)
  - freshness_lag_seconds: integer seconds between now() and freshness_as_of
  - freshness_status: one of [fresh, delayed, partial]
  - freshness_message: optional human-readable string (server-provided, short; UI may map to richer copy)
  - partial_reason_codes: optional comma-separated codes (e.g., LATE_EVENTS, REGION_INGESTION_GAP, BACKFILL_IN_PROGRESS)

Thresholds:
- Warning threshold to start: 20 minutes lag for hosted; 60 minutes for private deployments (verify with Logan/Nadia on realistic SLOs). If we can’t vary by deployment yet, start with a single default of 30 minutes.
- Treat “partial” as higher severity than “delayed” (banner should say results may change).

UI placement:
- Header row, right side: “Data as of …” + tooltip (“Aggregations update periodically; totals may shift as late events arrive.”)
- Banners below header and above filters; dismissible per session (local state) but reappear if severity increases.

Testing approach:
- Add mock responses in frontend tests for: fresh, delayed, partial.
- Add backend unit test ensuring freshness fields are always present (even for empty datasets).

Open questions:
- Should freshness be per workspace+project or per query slice (route/model)? Currently proposing per query slice but computed at aggregation dataset granularity.
- How to represent partial for sub-filters (e.g., specific model) if the partialness is only known at partition level.

Notes from incidents:
- During the timeout incident, customers saw spinning + retries; freshness banner should not require extra API call—reuse query response to avoid additional latency.

comments: Paula Mendes (2026-02-13): Please avoid implying billing is wrong. Suggest wording: ‘Usage Insights updates periodically; recent usage may be delayed. Totals can change as late events are processed.’

Logan Wright (2026-02-14): Partialness is easiest to compute at partition level (workspace/project/day). For now, return partial if ANY partition in requested range is marked incomplete. We can refine later.

Allison Grant (2026-02-15): Ensure the banner is driven by server metadata, not heuristic client comparisons. Also, add a small ‘learn more’ link to the help article so support can point customers somewhere consistent.
Dylan Brooks (2026-02-18): Keep extra calls out of the critical path. Freshness should ride along with the same response as the breakdown table query.
Dev Patel (2026-02-19): Support request: include partial reason code in internal debug panel (not customer-facing) so we can triage quickly when a customer says ‘it’s partial’.
Marcus Lin (2026-02-20): Export metadata is good; just ensure it does not leak internal region names for private deployments. Keep reason codes generic.
Marissa Cole (2026-02-25): OK to ship with single threshold for beta; we’ll revisit per-deployment thresholds for GA.
definition_of_done: Merged backend + frontend changes; freshness metadata included in all relevant endpoints; UI shows timestamp and banners; export includes timestamp; tests cover stale/partial states; copy approved by PM/DevEx; shipped behind beta flag with no additional query latency regression beyond 5%.
